title: Steve Owens and the 1969 Heisman: OU's Workhorse Running Back
question: When did Steve Owens win the Heisman Trophy and what were his stats?
answer: Steve Owens won the 1969 Heisman Trophy after leading the nation in rushing with 1,523 yards and in scoring with 138 points. He was Oklahoma's second Heisman winner, after Billy Vessels.
summary: Steve Owens won the 1969 Heisman after leading the nation with 1,523 rushing yards, then became a Lions star, OU athletic director and Norman businessman.
body: If any Sooner defined the word workhorse, it was Steve Owens. Born in Gore and raised in Miami, Oklahoma, he played three varsity seasons in Norman from 1967 through 1969 and left as one of the most productive runners college football had seen.

His 1969 senior year earned him the Heisman Trophy, the second in school history. Owens carried 358 times for 1,523 yards and 23 rushing touchdowns, leading the country in both rushing and scoring with 138 points. Against Oklahoma State that year he carried 55 times for 261 yards in a 28-27 win, and those 55 carries stand as a school single-game record. Over his career he put together 17 straight 100-yard games, an NCAA record at the time. He edged Purdue quarterback Mike Phipps in the vote, 1,488 points to 1,334.

The Detroit Lions picked him in the first round of the 1970 draft, 19th overall. In 1971 he ran for 1,035 yards, becoming the first Lion to clear 1,000 in a season, and that year earned him a Pro Bowl trip. He was named All-Pro in 1971 and 1972 before a knee injury ended his playing days.

Owens came home and built a life in Norman. He founded Steve Owens Insurance, broadcast Sooner games on a radio network of some 300 stations, and served as OU's athletic director from 1996 to 1998. He has also been a familiar face for charities such as Ronald McDonald House. The College Football Hall of Fame inducted him in 1991, and the city of Miami named a street for him.
